title: How to connect to Dynamics 365 Business Central On-Premises in VS Code (Use the On-Premises version for customization)
summary: This post explains how to configure VS Code to connect to a Business Central On-Premises environment for AL development. It covers modifying the launch.json file with correct server settings, enabling Developer Services in the BC instance configuration, and verifying authentication methods.
key_points: Replace the default server and serverInstance in launch.json with the URL and instance name seen when opening the on-premises web client, or check them via Get-NAVServerInstance
Look up DeveloperServicesPort in CustomSettings.config and add it as the port in launch.json; set DeveloperServicesEnabled to true, or use Set-NAVServerConfiguration
Restart the server instance after changing settings and make sure launch.json uses the right authentication, usually Windows on-premises
Do not build SaaS extensions against on-premises since some methods available on-premises are not usable in the cloud
From 2023 wave 1 the CRONUS demo license grants RIMDX on all objects, allowing AppSource apps to be run on-premises for testing
